quest.title: The Origin of the Lanterns
quest.description: On the day of the first full moon each year, the people of Liyue celebrate Lantern Rite. At nighttime, everyone in Liyue releases Xiao Lanterns and the Mingxiao Lantern into the bright night sky. Each Xiao Lantern contains a piece of Plaustrite that makes it float, and people hang wish sticks from them, which carry their hearts' desires in written or painted form. The lanterns slowly fly away, carrying the hope that the light they emit might guide the souls of Liyue's faithful protectors home, that they might return and be reunited with their people once more. You and Paimon arrive in Liyue as the festival is in full swing, preparing to enjoy yourselves...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Lantern Rite is nearly here, why don't we decorate the inn this year...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Lantern Rite"?

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Oh! Don't you know? On the first full moon of the first month each year, Liyue celebrates the Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: It's a festival to commemorate the heroes from the past. After dark, the people release Xiao and Mingxiao Lanterns into the night sky.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Ah... "May the flames of wisdom spread to all, and never be extinguished." This is the meaning of the lanterns. We believe they act as the beacons in the night, guiding bygone heroes back to their homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... It sounds like a grand festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And where there's a grand festival, there's always special seasonal snacks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you catch Paimon's drift?

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: You want to get involved in the Lantern Rite? That's great! The festive period leading up to the day itself is all part of the celebrations.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Haha... During this time, we pray to bring peace and ward off bad luck. Liyue locals call it "bidding farewell to the old and welcoming the new."

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: If you're looking to take part, it's not too late.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Oh, um... also...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Also what?

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: If you're able to... ahem... could you... try to convince Xiao to go with you?

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: We're not close, I wouldn't know how to ask him myself. But it seems that you've grown familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still, given his current mood...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon thinks it might be best to leave him alone for a few days...

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: I suppose you're right... Anyway! Just thought I'd mention it. You should get yourselves down to <color=#00E1FFFF>the harbor</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: If you leave too late, the city will be crowded with people, and you won't be able to make the most of it.

dialogues.speaker: Verr Goldet
dialogues.text: Get going! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: I'm Changchang, I just donated Dolly. She's my ragdoll.

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: Last night in my dream, Dolly told me her wish was to fly up into the sky and see the view.

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: So I gave her to the lady over by the big deer lantern. Dolly's wish will come true now, won't it?

dialogues.speaker: Changchang
dialogues.text: I did the right thing, didn't I? Wishes are supposed to come true at the Lantern Rite, aren't they?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: This year's Mingxiao Lantern is dedicated to Skybracer... He always was a show off — I'm sure he will be very pleased!

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: This year's Mingxiao Lantern will be the spitting image of him when it's complete!

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Well, that's the plan. I do hope they make the antlers big enough, they were his pride and joy after all.

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: The story goes that the antlers were made from the very essence of Rex Lapis' divine power, which made it the hardest material in all of Liyue.

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: But then, that fateful battle happened... The gods exchanged powerful blows, and the mountains started collapsing. To avoid impacting the villagers at the foot of the mountain, the adeptus got his friend to chop his antlers off...

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: He used those blood-drenched antlers as a wedge to prop up the mountain. And if that wasn't enough of a sacrifice, he then kept on fighting until his blood was drained and his life ran out...

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Thanks to him, Mt. Tianheng still stands tall and proud to this day. And the blood that he lost in the battle turned into the Bishui River.

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Hehehe... Whether you believe the story or not, I'm just happy you're willing to listen to me tell it.

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Surely, the reason the Lantern Rite exists is because people throughout the ages have chosen to come together as friends rather than stay in isolation.

response.speaker: Madame Ping
response.text: Goodbye. May the flames of wisdom spread to all, and never be extinguished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}! That stone is floating! Luckily, it's tethered in place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If it wasn't held down, who knows where it would fly off to?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: This is the Plaustrite to be used for the Mingxiao Lantern. The whole of the Xiao Market is centered around it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hello. Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: I'm Jiangzhou. Recently, I've been tracking progress on the construction of the Mingxiao Lantern.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: You seem like newcomers — is this your first Lantern Rite?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes... How can you tell?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: Well, I don't remember running into any weird and wonderful mascots at last year's festival.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is the Mingxiao Lantern, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: You'll see lots of people releasing little lanterns during the festival — those ones are called Xiao Lanterns. But there's also a huge one, a joint effort by all the people of Liyue Harbor. That one is called the Mingxiao Lantern.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: Almost every business in Liyue has a booth at the annual Xiao Market — but despite its popularity, this is the one time of the year they're not looking to make a profit. The street market exists solely to raise the funds and materials required for the Mingxiao Lantern construction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this Xiao Market... Does it have stuff you can eat?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: Plenty! And if I do say so myself, the Lantern Rite is the best festival for sampling Liyue's local delicacies.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: It is Liyue's biggest annual festival, after all. Showing off your craft is a great way to drum up a reputation.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: So, even if there's no Mora to be made, everyone is secretly going all out to get their produce under the spotlight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Folks in Liyue are so smart...

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: If you need any help, you can look for <color=#00E1FFFF>Wang'ya</color>, she's overseeing the Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: She's usually somewhere around the Xiao Market, she's your first port of call.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, will she know which stall sells the tastiest stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Jiangzhou
dialogues.text: No doubt. When it comes to the Lantern Rite, no one knows more than she does.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Got it! {NICKNAME}, let's go to the Xiao Market and look for <color=#00E1FFFF>Wang'ya</color>!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then... go to the stall with the tastiest food and eat till we're stuffed!

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hi, can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Huh, from the look of you, you don't hail from Liyue... Are you traveling through? Welcome to the Xiao Market.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you overseeing Lantern Rite?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Overseeing... Not exactly. The Lantern Rite festival belongs to the whole of Liyue, it's not just one person's to oversee.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I'm just taking care of a few small things. Doing my bit to make sure everyone who joins in the festivities has a good time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got a few things I'd like to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to know where the tastiest food in the whole wide Xiao Market is!

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hmm... the tastiest? Hard to say, I guess that depends on your personal preference. Still, what I can tell you is that everyone's talking about <color=#00E1FFFF>Yi'nian's</color> stall.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: If it gets any busier over there, I'm going to have to bring the Millelith to keep things orderly.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hey, you'd best get over there quick before the streets get too crowded with people.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Oh, and if you are heading to Yi'nian, please do me a favor and run this document over to him.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: It's a summary of the data from last year's Lantern Rite, compiled by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. It has a few operational tips for our vendors. If you're heading in that direction, it'd be a great help.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: As thanks, I've got a gift for you, when you get back.

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: We really don't have enough hands on deck, if I'd known, I would've roped some others in...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the best thing on the menu!?

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: Ah, customers. Take a look and decide for yourself. I can do anything on the menu. Or if there's something in particular you're after, I can do that instead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woo-hoo! Paimon'll have...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Now that you mention it, you do have a lot of options for a food stall...

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: Naturally! If there's a dish I can't cook, I've yet to hear about it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a document from Wang'ya.

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: Aha, same every year... the ol' operational tips! How's this for a tip — leave the handbook to one side and concentrate on the killer cooking!

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: Ugh, hand it over. I'll use it to feed the fire later.

dialogues.speaker: Yi'nian
dialogues.text: Come on then, place your orders, aren't ya here to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many... This one looks good, but Paimon wants to try that one too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Grilled Tiger Fish? That's the one Pervases loved to eat, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Seeing as the Lantern Rite is about commemorating the heroes of the past, let's order this one. This can be our way of honoring his memory.

choices.text: You mean your way of ordering your dinner...

response.speaker: Yi'nian
response.text: Ah, your friend has a good eye for food. That's our specialty.

response.speaker: Yi'nian
response.text: Please wait, I'll have it ready for you in no time.

response.speaker: Yi'nian
response.text: Okay! Here's your Grilled Tiger Fish. What do you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, delicious!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon's an expert in eating...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! What kind of a guide would Paimon be otherwise?

response.speaker: Yi'nian
response.text: Hahaha — well, hope you enjoy your food. I gotta see to some other customers.

response.speaker: Yi'nian
response.text: If you get hungry again, you know where I am!

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: So you're back, what do you think? Yi'nian makes some mean grub, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh, soooo tasty!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He said he wouldn't look at the document...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? ...He said that last year, too... If he'd listened to our marketing tips, he'd be doing even better by now.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Anyway, not to worry. Here's the gift I was talking about. This Xiao Lantern is for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Such a beautiful lantern! How is it made?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Uh... I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to explain the process concisely.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: But if you're interested in Xiao Lanterns, you can ask <color=#00E1FFFF>Jingming</color> over there. He's in charge of both the Xiao and Mingxiao Lanterns.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he's responsible for the super-duper huge one too?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: That's right! He should be easy to find. Just over there, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we could make a Xiao Lantern for Xiao... maybe that would cheer him up a bit!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's find <color=#00E1FFFF>Jingming</color> and see what he has to say.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: At this rate... we should be able to meet the deadline...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you teach us how to make Xiao Lanterns?

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Teach you how to make Xiao Lanterns? Oh... you don't look like locals to me. Looking to try your hand at making your own?

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: I'll be happy to teach you. There's no one way to make a Xiao Lantern, but let me start by showing you the simplest one.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: I should have some spare materials over here... Uh, just a second! Ah, they still need a bit of work. Take these, and give it a go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was so complicated... Paimon is all out of brain juice. Did you get it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just about...

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Hahaha, it all comes with practice. No one's expecting your first try to be perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Folks like you who want to learn my craft are a rare find nowadays...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you build that humongous Mingxiao Lantern using this same method?

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: That one? ...Hmm, I suppose it's fair to say the method is the same — broadly speaking. But no single person can take credit for it. The whole of Liyue comes together to make it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So it was a community effort?

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Surely you've heard about it? The Xiao Market is actually a fundraiser, aiming to support the Mingxiao Lantern's construction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... So that's how the Mingxiao Lantern is built...

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Such is the Lantern Rite tradition. The Ministry of Civil Affairs might be covering the bulk of the costs, but it's the citizens of Liyue that donate the materials, among many other things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh... So that's what that little girl meant when she said she'd donated her rag doll.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But since when do you build Mingxiao Lanterns out of rag dolls?

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Well, the Lantern Rite is a major festival. If somebody wants to make a contribution, no matter how small...

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: ...Or in this case, symbolic, we tend not to reject them. All well-meaning contributions are gratefully received.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Especially considering how grand of an occasion Lantern Rite is for everyone. People believe that joining the effort might bring them good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Heh, alrighty then. Shouldn't you get going? With all that the festival has to offer, I'm sure you must be on a busy schedule.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Of course, if you want to make another Xiao Lantern at any time, you know where to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite! Have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: So, did you find Jingming?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We did, and he taught us all about how to make Xiao Lanterns!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though Paimon can't really remember any of it...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hehe, no worries! You can always ask Jingming if you need to refresh your memory.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I should go, duty calls! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Bolai
dialogues.text: #Young {M#man}{F#lady}, if I may be so bold. How much for the floating thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not for sale!

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: Hahaha... As a matter of fact, I'm having some financial trouble recently. I probably couldn't afford it.

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: I'm just a small-time merchant anyway, I don't deal in rare and exotic treasures.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, the more you talk, the more suspicious you sound...

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: My, someone's in a grumpy mood aren't they? Here, maybe some candy will make you feel better?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ooh, suspiciously trustworthy!

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: So, I assume you two are in Liyue for the Lantern Rite?

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: This year's Mingxiao Lantern is supposed to be a sight well worth the wait. The Plaustrite that will lift the lantern into the air is the largest in twenty years!

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: It's big enough to make you wonder... if the fabled floating city in the clouds really does exist...

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: I guess it must just be held up by a similarly sized chunk of Plaustrite.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds awesome!

response.speaker: Bolai
response.text: Haha! I hope our paths cross again. Welcome to Liyue! ...Well, I can't speak for the whole of <color=#00E1FFFF>Liyue Harbor</color>, but you're always welcome in my store at least!

choices.text: Trust me, you couldn't afford it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a strange thing to say!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon's curious... What number did you have in mind, exactly?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, forget it. Let's assume you meant Paimon is worth more than Mora can buy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, typical Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: You better get going if you want to get to <color=#00E1FFFF>Yi'nian's</color> food stall. It'll be packed soon!

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: If you're interested in Xiao Lanterns, you can ask <color=#00E1FFFF>Jingming</color> over there. He's in charge of both our Xiao and Mingxiao Lanterns.

dialogues.speaker: Jingming
dialogues.text: Building materials... Yes, this seems to be enough... Ah, and I still have these...
